_source: Hand-curated from internal/gateway/connector setup paths and hook profiles plus cli/defenseclaw/inventory/hook_contracts.json. Re-extract on every connector or hook-contract change.
_order: By adoption / popularity — mirrors the hero rotation (lib/hero-connectors.ts) and the docs nav (content/docs/connectors/meta.json).

connectors.label: Claude Code
connectors.summary: Native lifecycle hooks, native approval, and OpenTelemetry export.
connectors.hilt: Claude Code supports native PreToolUse ask prompts. CRITICAL findings still block; HIGH findings can pause for approval.
connectors.notes: Hook-only connector — no proxy data path and no DefenseClaw subprocess sandbox or command shims. Observability and PreToolUse deny decisions both flow through the hook bus.

connectors.label: Codex
connectors.summary: Config hooks, native OpenTelemetry, and an agent-turn completion bridge.
connectors.hilt: Codex has no native ask surface here; confirm becomes an alert/systemMessage with raw_action preserved. The TUI can review the event but cannot resume it.
connectors.notes: Three telemetry channels at boot: hooks, native OTel, and the notify bridge for agent-turn-complete events. Hook-only connector — no proxy data path and no DefenseClaw subprocess sandbox or command shims.

connectors.label: OpenClaw
connectors.summary: Reference proxy with bundled fetch interception and before-tool-call enforcement.
connectors.hilt: OpenClaw supports DefenseClaw approval prompts for tool actions. Approvals reach chat-origin sessions via the bundled plugin.
connectors.notes: Reference proxy connector — full data-path interception, sandbox enforcement, plugin-mediated HITL.

connectors.label: Cursor
connectors.summary: Pre-execution shell and MCP hooks with native ask support.
connectors.hilt: Cursor enforces native ask only on beforeShellExecution and beforeMCPExecution. preToolUse accepts ask in the schema but does not enforce it.
connectors.notes: hooks.json under ~/.cursor; command hooks fail open by default and use failClosed=true only for an explicit closed failure mode. sessionStart/sessionEnd are fire-and-forget and Stop is followup-only. Native Windows uses the managed PowerShell stdin adapter.

connectors.label: Hermes
connectors.summary: Preview native lifecycle hooks with valid-JSON pre-tool blocking and unconditional failure-open behavior.
connectors.hilt: Hermes has no native human-approval surface; confirm verdicts are recorded and alerted but cannot pause or resume the hook.
connectors.notes: Preview/not certified on native Windows. Hooks live in %HERMES_HOME%/config.yaml (default %LOCALAPPDATA%/hermes; hermes-hooks-v1 >=0.19.0). The owned command is a directly quoted absolute native defenseclaw-hook.exe argv parsed by shlex.split and run with shell=False; DefenseClaw uses no shell wrapper. All 23 Hermes v0.19 VALID_HOOKS events are registered and classified independently. Only valid synchronous pre_tool_call block JSON vetoes a tool; pre_llm_call may inject context and pre_verify may continue a bounded verification loop. Transform, API, gateway, approval, Kanban, and ordinary lifecycle events are audit-only in DefenseClaw's shell lane unless the official shell parser proves an effect. Timeout, nonzero exit, malformed output, authentication, and transport failures warn and continue; exit status is not enforcement. Hermes's separate upstream terminal tool uses installer-managed PortableGit/Git Bash on Windows and is outside DefenseClaw integration. Discovery surfaces cover MCP, skills, and read-only plugins.

connectors.label: OpenCode
connectors.summary: Auto-loaded bridge plugin with tool-execution blocking.
connectors.hilt: No native human-approval surface; blocks by throwing in the bridge plugin's tool.execute.before. confirm verdicts fall back to allow.
connectors.notes: Native Windows is preview pending integrated packaged Setup and pinned official-client validation. Governed by a DefenseClaw JS bridge plugin auto-loaded from OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR/plugins/defenseclaw.js or the default ~/.config/opencode/plugins/defenseclaw.js (no opencode.json edit). tool.execute.before POSTs to /api/v1/opencode/hook and throws new Error(reason) to abort the tool on a block decision; tool.execute.after is best-effort observe-only. Fail-closed applies only to the awaited before hook: the bridge throws there when the gateway is unreachable and FAIL_MODE=closed.

connectors.label: OmniGent
connectors.summary: Custom policy bridge with allow, ask, and deny enforcement.
connectors.hilt: OmniGent parks request, tool_call, and llm_request for native ASK approval. Post-phase confirm findings are audited and continue without a pause; DENY may suppress onward-visible content but cannot roll back completed work.
connectors.notes: The documented custom Python policy bridge maps all six OmniGent policy phases. Post-phase DENY uses OmniGent's denial/sentinel behavior rather than custom replacement data. Native OTLP is inactive until the launch process exports the standard environment variables; OpenTelemetry packages are included in OmniGent's base/default dependency set.

connectors.label: Gemini CLI
connectors.summary: Settings hooks with a native OTLP exporter pointed at the gateway.
connectors.hilt: Can block supported hook events but has no native human-approval surface; confirm verdicts fall back explicitly.
connectors.notes: settings.json hooks; native OTLP exporter wires directly to the gateway.

connectors.label: GitHub Copilot CLI
connectors.summary: Global or workspace hooks with native approval on pre-tool-use.
connectors.hilt: Copilot CLI supports native ask on documented preToolUse hooks.
connectors.notes: Global hooks under ~/.copilot/hooks by default; optional workspace hooks under <workspace>/.github/hooks.

connectors.label: OpenHands
connectors.summary: Global command hooks with optional workspace-local discovery surfaces.
connectors.hilt: OpenHands has no native ask surface in the documented hook contract; confirm verdicts are downgraded with raw_action preserved and optional additionalContext returned to the agent.
connectors.notes: Global ~/.openhands/hooks.json native hook schema by default; optional repo-local .openhands/hooks.json with --workspace; MCP lives in ~/.openhands/mcp.json; skills include user installs and ~/.openhands/cache/skills/public-skills/skills.

connectors.label: Antigravity
connectors.summary: Five lifecycle hooks, with documented native ask on PreToolUse.
connectors.hilt: Antigravity documents native ask on PreToolUse only. DefenseClaw does not claim that this response overrides permission-bypass flags without persisted official-client evidence; force_ask is retained only as internal raw_action telemetry.
connectors.notes: DefenseClaw's v2 contract registers all five documented Antigravity lifecycle events (PreInvocation, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostInvocation, Stop) in ~/.gemini/config/hooks.json with their vendor-specific direct-list or matcher-group shapes. Only synchronous PreToolUse exposes documented hard deny and native ask decisions; invocation events are context-transform surfaces, PostToolUse is observe-only, and DefenseClaw returns allow for Stop rather than claiming stop blocking. MCP read/write uses ~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json and <workspace>/.agents/mcp_config.json. AgentSkills folder form is read/write at ~/.gemini/config/skills and <workspace>/.agents/skills. Plugins live at ~/.gemini/config/plugins or <workspace>/.agents/plugins; the CLI staging path is also discovered. Rules and standalone or plugin-contained agents remain discovery/scan only.

connectors.label: Windsurf
connectors.summary: Cascade hooks across prompts, commands, code access, and MCP tools.
connectors.hilt: Can block supported hook events but has no native human-approval surface; confirm verdicts fall back explicitly.
connectors.notes: Cascade hooks under ~/.codeium/windsurf/hooks.json. DefenseClaw can map its configured availability failures to Windsurf's blocking exit 2 on the five documented pre-hooks; Windsurf itself fails open on other non-zero exits. Post hooks are non-blocking, Cascade response post hooks are asynchronous, and Restricted Mode disables hooks. Existing MCP/rules are discovered, never auto-created.

connectors.label: ZeptoClaw
connectors.summary: API base redirect through the DefenseClaw proxy with response scanning.
connectors.hilt: ZeptoClaw has no native ask surface; confirm uses its explicit fallback with raw_action preserved for TUI/audit review. There is no resumable approval.
connectors.notes: api_base redirect into the DefenseClaw proxy plus response-scan.
